own_solution.law: Classical translational equipartition gives (1/2)M<v²> = (3/2)RT, so v_rms = sqrt(3RT/M). With M = 0.004 kg/mol and T = 300 K, v_rms = sqrt(1870650) = 1367.72 m/s.
assumptions: Classical equilibrium translational equipartition applies; this governing statistical model is not explicitly stated.
Speeds are measured relative to the gas's bulk rest frame.
After heating, the measured gas has equilibrated at 400 K.

defect_reasons.missing_assumption: The classical equilibrium statistical model needed to infer molecular rms speed from temperature and molar mass alone is unstated, contrary to the strict admission requirement for governing modelling conditions.
defect_reasons.rendering_not_minimal: T3A0A introduces a closed rigid container in addition to changing the wording of the temperature-rise statement.

notes: All numerical answers and role assignments are conditional on classical equilibrium equipartition. An ideal equation of state is not independently necessary: classical equilibrium translational equipartition also holds with position-dependent intermolecular interactions. Heating the sample by 100 K gives 400 K and multiplies its rms speed by sqrt(4/3). Holding the container rigid changes the heating process but not this final-temperature result. For either 2 mol sentence, (1/2)nM<v²> = (3/2)nRT shows explicitly that n cancels. All temperature-rise variants consistently specify 100 K, and both amount variants specify 2 mol. No added statement contradicts the base problem.
